questions.q: According to standard penal laws, the supreme punishment associated with the crime of Murder is:
questions.explain: In the Nigerian penal system, murder is a capital offence. The legally prescribed punishment upon conviction is the **death penalty**.
questions.exam: BECE National Values Education: Security Education
questions.subject: National Values Education

questions.q: What is the specific minimum prison term generally associated with the crime of Drug Trafficking according to penal classifications?
questions.explain: Standard civic and security education curricula stipulate **10 years imprisonment** as the associated benchmark punishment for offenders convicted of drug trafficking.
questions.exam: BECE National Values Education: Security Education
questions.subject: National Values Education

questions.q: A person found guilty of Human Trafficking is liable to a punishment of:
questions.explain: The crime of human trafficking carries severe penalties. The prescribed punishment typically falls within the range of **5 to 10 years imprisonment**.
questions.exam: BECE National Values Education: Security Education
questions.subject: National Values Education

questions.q: The most legally appropriate punishment prescribed for a person found guilty of Rape is:
questions.explain: **Rape** is a severe felony. Upon conviction, the offender is subjected to severe legal sanctions, most notably **imprisonment** (which can extend to life depending on aggravating factors).
questions.exam: BECE National Values Education: Security Education
questions.subject: National Values Education

questions.q: Which Nigerian agency is legally empowered to track, arrest, and prosecute offenders involved in Drug Trafficking?
options: National Agency for Food and Drug Administration and Control (NAFDAC)
questions.explain: The **NDLEA** (National Drug Law Enforcement Agency) is the federal agency in Nigeria tasked primarily with eliminating the growing, manufacturing, processing, trafficking, and exporting of hard drugs.
questions.exam: BECE National Values Education: Security Education
questions.subject: National Values Education

questions.q: The criminal act of secretly adding inferior, harmful, or cheaper substances to medical products is known as:
questions.explain: **Drug adulteration** involves altering a drug's original quality by adding inferior or toxic substances, thereby reducing its efficacy and endangering consumers' lives.
questions.exam: BECE National Values Education: Security Education
questions.subject: National Values Education

questions.q: If an individual is found guilty of theft by a court of competent jurisdiction, the associated legal punishment is usually:
questions.explain: For **theft**, the legally prescribed punitive measure is **imprisonment**. The duration of the imprisonment usually depends on the value of the stolen items and the circumstances.
questions.exam: BECE National Values Education: Security Education
questions.subject: National Values Education

questions.q: Which of the following bodies helps to curb the crime of Food and Drug Contamination in Nigeria?
questions.explain: The **National Agency for Food and Drug Administration and Control (NAFDAC)** regulates and controls the manufacture, importation, exportation, advertisement, distribution, sale, and use of food and drugs.
questions.exam: BECE National Values Education: Security Education
questions.subject: National Values Education

questions.q: Why does the law associate severe punishments like 5–10 years imprisonment with Human Trafficking?
options: To reduce the population of people in the country
To generate income for the government through bail money
To serve as a strong deterrence because the crime degrades human dignity and violates basic human rights
Because the police do not have enough holding cells
questions.explain: Associated punishments serve a dual purpose: penalizing the offender and **deterring** others. Human trafficking severely violates human rights, justifying its strict penal consequence of 5 to 10 years imprisonment.
